0a7f24e7607a8498: Google has patched its eighth actively exploited Chrome zero-day of 2026, matching its total for the whole of last year with nearly two months still left on the calendar.

The latest flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-125350, is a high-severity use-after-free vulnerability in Chrome's XML component. Google confirmed in a security advisory published Monday that attackers are already exploiting the bug, although it hasn't said who's behind the attacks or who might be getting targeted.
"Google is aware that an exploit for CVE-2026-125350 exists in the wild," the company said, offering little else about the attacks.

The vulnerability was reported anonymously on November 6 and involves a memory management error that occurs when software continues using a pointer to memory that has already been freed. Such bugs can potentially allow attackers to corrupt memory and execute malicious code, although Google hasn't disclosed how this particular flaw is being exploited.
Google is keeping further technical details under wraps until enough users have installed the fix, a familiar approach intended to stop other attackers from getting their hands on a working exploit.

The patch arrives in Chrome 157.0.8103.50/.51 for Windows and macOS, and 157.0.8103.50 for Linux. The update also addresses eight other security vulnerabilities, including high-severity flaws affecting WebGL, FileSystem, GPU, Compositing, and the V8 JavaScript engine.

The release fixes another use-after-free bug in Chrome's XML component, CVE-2026-125346, which was reported by Arni Hardarson of Neonix Security in October, though Google hasn't indicated that this second vulnerability is being exploited.

The latest discovery adds to what's becoming a rather long list of Chrome zero-days this year. By June, Google had already patched five actively exploited Chrome zero-days, including flaws in its V8 JavaScript engine, Skia graphics library, and WebGPU implementation. The list has only grown since then, with two more V8 bugs fixed in September and the latest XML vulnerability bringing the total to eight.

That puts 2026 level with 2025, when Google also fixed eight Chrome zero-days exploited in the wild. Whether the browser maker can make it through the remaining weeks of the year without adding another to the pile is anyone's guess.

Google says the latest update will roll out over the coming days and weeks, but users can check manually by heading to Chrome's Settings menu and selecting About Chrome. With attackers already making use of the vulnerability, it's probably worth doing that sooner rather than waiting for Chrome to get around to it. ®

497cb7273febfea1: GEORGE TOWN: Former Penang Development Corporation (PDC) general manager Datuk Seri Chet Singh Karam Singh, widely regarded as one of the architects of Penang's industrialisation, died this morning. He was 90.
His death was confirmed by his daughter, Surita Amreeth Karamsingh, when contacted.

Chet Singh's passing marks the end of an era for a man who, alongside the late former chief minister Tun Dr Lim Chong Eu, played a pivotal role in transforming Penang into the 'Silicon Valley of the East'.
Born in Kuala Kangsar, Perak, in 1936, Chet began his civil service career at the Defence Ministry before being appointed Penang State Financial Officer in late 1967.
Following the establishment of PDC after Penang lost its free port status, Chet was seconded to lead the corporation.
He served as its general manager for 20 years, from 1971 until his retirement in 1991.
Under his leadership, Penang underwent a rapid transformation from a state grappling with severe unemployment following the loss of its port status into an export-oriented industrial hub.

He played a key role in attracting multinational semiconductor companies, including National Semiconductor, AMD, Hewlett-Packard and Intel, to establish their pioneering offshore manufacturing operations in the Bayan Lepas Free Trade Zone.

By the time he retired in 1991, the state's industrial parks housed more than 500 manufacturing companies employing over 115,000 workers, reversing the economic decline and raising Penang's per capita income well above the national average.
According to a bereavement notice shared by Gurdwara Sahib Bayan Baru, the wake will be held tomorrow from 9.30am at his residence in Minden Heights, Gelugor.
Family members and friends may pay their final respects before the cortege departs at 2.15pm.
The funeral and last rites (saskar) will be held at the Batu Gantung Crematorium at 3pm.

8f873d564b72118e: Classes at Vanderbilt University are proceeding as scheduled today, although access to most university systems remains restricted following a cyberattack claimed by ransomware group BYOD.
Vanderbilt announced on Monday morning that it was dealing with "an active cybersecurity incident," and that the fallout may affect university devices, systems, and cloud-based services.

The Nashville-based university initially told students and staff to shut down university devices and disconnect from campus Wi-Fi. It warned them to watch for unexpected prompts, altered files or permissions, unfamiliar applications, and unsolicited authentication requests.
Campus computers reportedly began playing an audio threat attributed to BYOD. Student newspaper The Vanderbilt Hustler cited posts on campus social network Fizz showing the message.

"You have been compromised by BYOD," the recording said. "We suggest you reach out to us as soon as possible. Instructions have been placed on your desktop. Failure to communicate will result in this estate being brought to the ground completely. Make the right choice or rot with the wrong one."
By Monday evening, Vanderbilt had restored access to campus Wi-Fi, but warned that access to most systems remains restricted.

"We know this has disrupted important work and caused frustration across the university," it said. "Vanderbilt Information Technology is working with government agencies and other partners to manage this situation."
Students were told to attend classes as scheduled on Tuesday and contact instructors about flexibility on coursework deadlines. Staff were instructed to report to work normally.
Vanderbilt's Athletics department said that its ticketing system was unavailable, and that students were unable to claim tickets for the college's football game against Alabama on Saturday.
BYOD claimed responsibility for the attack on Vanderbilt on Monday, along with extensive data theft.
"If you could not tell already, your databases are locked [and] we have your entire estate and research data," it said via its leak site.
"Over 1 million SSNs, full names, email addresses, phone numbers, student and employee records, full takeover of your DC, whatever was on your network, we possess."
Vanderbilt has not confirmed BYOD's claims about the extent of its access or the data allegedly stolen.
BYOD may be a familiar name to some. The group previously claimed attacks on the University of New Mexico and Trump Mobile's customer database.
BYOD also claimed responsibility on Monday for an attack on Texas Health and Human Services. The agency has not publicly confirmed an incident and did not immediately respond to our questions. ®
4668ffcb5b4538a3: The metals industry has experienced transformational moments before: the Bessemer process, flash smelting, electric arc furnaces, and modern continuous casting all changed what was possible.

Yet, for more than a century, most extraction processes rely on techniques and pathways that would be familiar to metallurgists from generations ago. Processes have become larger and control systems smarter, but the fundamental science behind separating metals from ores has changed less than many realize.
Today’s materials challenges are different from those of the 20th century, but why are critical metals still produced using largely the same scientific foundations?

EvoMaterials, a technology platform developed by Outokumpu—the global leader in sustainable stainless steel and the producer of ferrochrome with 67% lower carbon footprint than the industry average—is exploring that question by rethinking how metals can be extracted:

“We decided to go beyond the current constraints and look fundamentally at what’s the best way to do this with the benefit of the scientific engineering knowledge and hindsight that we have today,” says Caspar Stinn, technical director for extractive metallurgy at Outokumpu. “We’re looking at how we can reimagine metals production.”
A supply chain problem disguised as a materials problem

As economies expand and the world becomes increasingly electrified, data and scientific models point to rising demand for many minerals, driven by technologies ranging from data centers to aerospace, water treatment, energy systems, and defence. According to Antoine Allanore, professor of metallurgy at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) this coincides with many Western economies having reduced their domestic processing capacity for the very metals those industries depend on.
Metallurgy is now strategically important, shaped not only by cost and availability but also by carbon footprint, geographic origin and supply-chain resilience.

That reality is particularly relevant for chromium and other specialty metals used in high-temperature and extreme environments. Chromium-based materials play a critical role in aerospace systems, power generation, corrosion-resistant infrastructure and defense technologies, where materials must perform under demanding conditions.
Beyond optimization

For decades, metallurgical innovation largely focused on improving yields, energy efficiency and process control. EvoMaterials is based on the idea that some metallurgical processes may benefit from entirely different chemical pathways.

The platform originates from research into sulfidation-based processing technologies, initially pursued to reduce carbon emissions associated with ferrochrome production. Laboratory work revealed broader potential.

Lab-scale trials demonstrated that these alternative process chemistries could potentially do more than lower emissions. They could recover valuable metals from lower grade resources and industrial side streams while fundamentally altering how separation processes are performed. The opportunity is to rethink how mineral resources are used and how much value can be extracted from them, bringing in greater resource efficiency and stronger industrial competitiveness.
Understanding traditional smelting vs. new proprietary technology

Development of the technology began in the United States in 2021 for chromite from Outokumpu’s Kemi mine in Finland, the only chrome mine in the European Union and one of the few such operations across the Western world. Since then, Outokumpu has evolved the technology through extensive research and development, combining new process chemistries with proprietary metallurgical expertise, supported in part by a non-exclusive patent license agreement from MIT.

“The technology is a new application for separating metallic elements from materials,” explains Allanore. Historically, that separation has been achieved using carbon- and energy-intensive approaches. The new method creates a different chemical environment that enables more efficient extraction with fewer losses and fewer unwanted by-products, recovering critical materials from resources considered waste.
Innovation happens at the boundaries

EvoMaterials sits at the intersection of several scientific disciplines, a combination that strongly resonates with Stinn, who completed his PhD in Materials Science and Engineering at MIT, where his research focused on low-carbon metals processing and recycling technologies.

Modern materials innovation draws on a growing mix of chemistry, materials science, physics, computational modeling, and engineering. With advanced simulation tools and AI helping researchers identify promising directions, scientific discovery still depends on experimentation and testing in the lab—on getting your hands dirty and doing the hard work.

“Science today is much more interdisciplinary than it was, and the collaboration across disciplines reveals new scientific opportunities,” says Stinn. Engineering can translate those opportunities into more efficient and cost-competitive metals production.
Building a technology platform

A technically significant aspect of EvoMaterials is that it’s not a single process, but a technology platform. Allanore compares EvoMaterials to platform technologies in other industries, where a single scientific breakthrough can enable multiple downstream applications.

Once a new extraction pathway has been mastered for one material system, the same scientific principles may be adapted to entirely different metals and mineral resources. The initial application becomes only the starting point.
“The future and the potential impact might be much broader than the original and current developments that are happening,” Allanore explains.
That possibility is increasingly important as industries seek secure supplies of nickel, chromium, molybdenum, and other strategic materials needed for advanced manufacturing.
The future of materials companies

The broader implication extends beyond metallurgy. Companies that develop proprietary process technologies may create value through production but also through intellectual property and scientific expertise.

Based on Outokumpu’s technology leadership, that transition could create entirely new categories of value, enabling the production of high-value critical materials from ores and resource streams that previously appeared uneconomical or inaccessible.

The result would be a fundamental shift in how metals are manufactured, where sustainability, resource efficiency, supply security, and economic value become outcomes of the same technological architecture rather than separate objectives.

The next step for EvoMaterials is pilot-scale validation, with a pilot plant in New Hampshire to begin operations in the first half of 2027. The facility will scale the proprietary technology from laboratory to one-ton production, providing a step toward industrial-scale deployment targeted for 2030. Beyond producing low-CO2, chromium-enriched ferrochrome and chromium metal, the platform could be adapted to other strategic materials, including nickel and molybdenum.
The work raises a broader question—how many of today’s metallurgical processes would look the same if they were invented from scratch? Or could those routes be designed differently today?
The next revolution in materials may begin by rethinking how to extract the metals that society depends on.
This content was produced by Outokumpu. It was not written by MIT Technology Review’s editorial staff.

bec92a3f7ebc2f5d: BRATISLAVA: The Czech and Slovak prime ministers on Tuesday slammed German Chancellor Friedrich Merz for urging "a collective commitment" by fellow European Union members to help fund Ukraine.

Merz has said in a letter seen by AFP that the EU needs to agree on funding to keep Ukraine going next year as it keeps battling a Russian invasion before the bloc can resolve a standoff over the next budget.
Brussels has said Kyiv is facing a €70 billion (US$78 billion) shortfall in 2027, of which the 27-nation EU should look to cover some €45 billion.

Merz told EU chief Antonio Costa in the letter first reported by the Financial Times that "a collective commitment that all of us, without exception, will contribute fairly to closing this gap is an essential prerequisite for resolving this issue".
"What the chancellor is doing is typical blackmail, and I will not give in to it," Slovakia's nationalist prime minister Robert Fico told reporters in Bratislava.
"We are a sovereign country... (and) we have our own opinion on the matter."
Fico, who fosters close ties with the Kremlin, has rejected direct military aid to Ukraine.

Visiting Bratislava on Tuesday, Czech prime minister Andrej Babis, whose nationalist government also rejects military aid to Ukraine, dismissed Merz's comment, citing the EU's overall support for Ukraine.
"I do not know why he is saying it," Babis said.

The EU last year came up with a €90 billion loan for Ukraine, but as Russia has stepped up its bombardments of Ukraine's infrastructure, it has become increasingly clear that those funds will run out before the end of next year.
Both Prague and Bratislava negotiated an exemption from guarantees for the loan.
European diplomats and EU officials say they expect the bloc to agree to a new loan for Ukraine modelled around the earlier €90 billion one.
Merz asked Costa to add the matter to the agenda of an EU leaders' meeting in Dublin on Friday.

f30dae78bead60f3: KUALA LUMPUR: Peguam Najib Razak, Shafee Abdullah berkata, hanya mahkamah yang mempunyai bidang kuasa untuk merangka perintah membabitkan kes jenayah.

e4c8ab71581719cc: Between 12 and 13 million UK smart meters could stop working properly when 2G and 3G networks are switched off by 2033, and replacing them all is likely to cost around £4 billion ($5.3 billion).
Smart meters have long been a controversial topic thanks to the British government's botched rollout of the technology; they were supposed to be fitted into 80 percent of households by 2020.
But numerous delays and technical hitches, such as consumers finding their meter stopped being smart if they switched energy supplier, hindered progress.

Now, a report from connectivity biz Wirepas, "The European Connectivity Trilemma," shows that it isn't just Brits who have problems, but that other European countries also have their share of smart meter issues and that no two countries have adopted the same approach.

The UK's issues center on the fact that early meters used 2G or 3G cellular connections to transmit energy usage back to the supplier. These continued to be fitted until 4G versions began arriving at the end of 2024, the report says.
This issue was covered by The Register back in 2023, and again in 2024.

However, the government had already announced measures to phase out 2G and 3G networks by 2033 several years earlier, back in 2021, so it was known that any meters being fitted would have a limited lifespan.

In fact, 3G services have now already been withdrawn by the networks, and they all plan to phase out 2G ahead of the 2033 deadline. BT/EE will begin closing its network from May 2029, VMO2 will start the same summer, and Vodafone aims to switch off in spring 2030.

The report claims the UK now faces two substantial areas of expenditure as a result. The first covers newer, second generation (SMETS2) meters, where only the communications module needs swapping out, but even this is likely to cost £1.3 to £1.4 billion (c $1.7 to $1.9 billion) before the hardware cost of each new hub is even factored in.

The other is for an estimated 7 million older, first-generation (SMETS1) meter installations, which have the cellular comms hard-wired in, so the whole meter typically needs replacing. The report authors estimate this will cost another £2.1 billion to £2.45 billion ($2.8 billion to $3.3 billion), at an indicative replacement cost of £300 to £350 per installation.
This results in the estimated £4 billion in gross replacement costs, which will ultimately feed into household energy bills, adding to the very costs the government is currently trying to reduce.
We asked the Department for Energy Security and Net Zero (DESNZ), which oversees smart meters, for comment.

While some of these older meters would naturally have been due for replacement as part of normal asset renewal cycles, the cell network shutdown makes the replacement program unavoidable and dictates when much of the expenditure must occur.

According to the report, the SMETS2 replacement largely applies to central and southern Britain, as second-gen meters in the north use a long-range radio network and are not subject to the 2G/3G cut-off. However, the issue of older SMETS1 meters applies nationwide.

Wirepas' interest in all of this is that it specializes in IoT connectivity and is pushing NR+ as a solution to the issue. Based on the DECT-2020 New Radio standard developed by the European Telecommunication Standards Institute (ETSI), this is designed to be scalable and operates in the license-exempt and globally available 1.9GHz part of the spectrum.

When 4G technology reaches the end of its life, (which isn't likely to happen until the 2040s, and there is no planned date) the UK's smart meters will need to be replaced once again, the report asserts. However, this is sufficiently far in the future that it is unlikely to trouble policymakers anytime soon. ®

d0668873570f9996: KUALA LUMPUR: DAP Deputy National Publicity Secretary Hannah Yeoh has expressed regret over Anthony Loke's decision to resign as Transport Minister with immediate effect today.

"I should have been the one to resign today, but my secretary-general wanted us to fulfil all our promises to the people and complete the work that remains unfinished.

b33c400d1e3403ea: SUNGAI PETANI: A 42-year-old man was found unconscious before being pronounced dead at a mental health care and treatment centre in Taman Kempas, here, last night.

“Investigations at the scene revealed that the victim, Zulkiflee Zainuddin, was found unconscious before being pronounced dead.

24f0445a9e94698f: KUALA LUMPUR: Next week's Hong Kong Open will be the final opportunity for Leong Jun Hao to prove to BAM that he can still compete at the highest level.

National singles coaching director Kenneth Jonassen said they will evaluate the world No. 32 Jun Hao, taking into account his results, attitude, willingness to learn and contribution towards helping younger players.
Jun Hao withdrew from this week's Kumamoto Masters in Japan to have more time to prepare for the Hong Kong Open (Nov 17-22).
Jonassen said Jun Hao needs to demonstrate that he can secure at least two consecutive wins at the Hong Kong Open, having frequently stumbled in the second rounds.
He said reaching the quarter-finals serves as a crucial benchmark in assessing a player's capability to compete with the world's elite in any given tournament.
"Throughout this season, we have seen him clear the first round several times, only to get stuck in the second round," Jonassen said today.
"So, the objective is to overcome that hurdle. We need to see him deliver two high-quality performances back-to-back — not just playing well, but actually securing the victories."
Jun Hao has endured a challenging season, failing to reach the quarter-finals in all 12 World Tour tournaments he entered this year.
He also suffered early exits at the Asian Badminton Championships, the World Championships, and the singles event at the Aichi-Nagoya 2026 Asian Games.
Jonassen added that the evaluation of Jun Hao would extend beyond court results, encompassing his attitude, commitment to self-improvement, and contribution to the national training environment.

"All these factors are important when evaluating a player at Jun Hao's stage and age. Once a player reaches his level of experience, we aren't just looking for good performances — we also expect wins."
9a8e1caa94681259: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 10 — Datin Seri Rosmah Mansor has expressed gratitude following the return of her husband, former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak, to their residence in Jalan Langgak Duta here today after a court order allowing him to serve the remainder of his sentence under house detention.

af36f97a3ec4dc3a: BEIJING: Not getting enough sleep can take a toll on our health. For celebrities who spend long hours filming, often through the night, the consequences can be particularly worrying.
One such person is Chinese actor Hu Ge.
The 44-year-old recently opened up about his health concerns on the Chinese medical talk show Healing Encounters, revealing that he now takes extra precautions because of problems with his heart.
He is so concerned that he carries emergency heart medication with him wherever he goes, and he also brings an automated external defibrillator (AED) whenever he travels for work.
The actor, who has also quit smoking due to his heart condition, admitted that he initially found carrying the device rather inconvenient.
But he eventually realised it could come in handy if someone else needed emergency help.
"At first, I thought it was quite troublesome, but then I realised that if someone else were to experience a medical emergency, I could use it to help them too," he said.
Hu recalled spending more than three years filming the Chinese drama Blossoms Shanghai, with 60 to 70 per cent of the scenes shot at night.

The demanding schedule left him physically exhausted throughout production. He admitted that he began noticing a decline in his physical condition after turning 40—whereas in the past, he could bounce back from a night of filming simply by catching up on sleep.

Things became even more concerning after he spent seven months filming the 2026 drama Born to Be Alive in high-altitude regions. A medical check-up after he returned revealed abnormalities involving his heart and other areas.
The findings were a wake-up call for Hu, who now believes people should not wait until their health deteriorates before taking action.

"We often only start addressing our health when something goes wrong. But what I've come to realise is that everyone should take primary responsibility for their own life and health, rather than waiting until something happens before seeking medical attention," he said.
Hu added: "Health and life are like credit cards. When you're young, you keep overspending without thinking about having to pay it back. But now, it's time to start settling the bill."
6d1893c4016ceb1b: SEREMBAN: Police have arrested a Chinese national who allegedly abandoned his son by the road, leading the boy to cling to the back of their car before falling near the Nilai toll plaza.

Nilai police chief Johari Yahya said the man, 45, was arrested at a residence in Jalan Cheras, Kuala Lumpur, at about 12.15pm. Police also seized a white Perodua Axia involved in the incident which went viral on social media.
"The man admitted to being involved in the incident and said he and his family had gone to Pantai Bagan Lalang, Selangor, via the North South Expressway at about 1pm yesterday.

"During the journey, the 12-year-old boy, his eldest son, angered the man by arguing with his second child. He stopped the car at the roadside, ordered the victim out and scolded him," he said in a statement.
The man then left the victim by the roadside and continued driving, claiming he wanted to teach his son a lesson so that he would not repeat his actions.

Johari said the suspect claimed to have seen the victim fall onto the road after he continued driving, prompting him to turn back to pick up his son before taking him to a private clinic in Bandar Baru Nilai.
The case is being investigated under Section 31(1)(a) of the Child Act 2001 for child neglect or abandonment.
6c00601b01b3411e: GEORGE TOWN, Nov 10 — Penang police are awaiting further instructions from the Deputy Public Prosecutor (DPP) on the investigation into an allegation that a state assemblyman injured his wife in an incident on October 31.

9a64c154f2fb8bcc: MELAKA: Presiden Umno Zahid Hamidi menggesa agar tiada lagi polemik berhubung tahanan rumah bekas perdana menteri Najib Razak susulan keputusan Mahkamah Tinggi hari ini.

Zahid diminta mengulas keputusan Mahkamah Tinggi Kuala Lumpur mengeluarkan perintah baharu yang membenarkan Najib menjalani baki hukuman penjaranya bagi sabitan kes rasuah di bawah tahanan rumah berkuat kuasa serta-merta.
Beliau turut melahirkan harapan agar Najib dapat meluangkan masa bersama keluarganya.

Loke mengumumkan peletakan jawatannya sebagai menteri pengangkutan pada September selepas Najib diberikan pengampunan bersyarat, namun berkata peletakan jawatan itu hanya akan berkuat kuasa apabila Najib mula menjalani hukuman penjara bagi kes SRC di bawah tahanan rumah.
cd6c2c30416498af: BUKIT KAYU HITAM: Nearly 25 tonnes of frozen chicken worth RM562,290 were seized by the Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (MCBA) after the importer was found to have submitted an expired import permit.
The seizure followed a physical inspection by MCBA officers at the Bilik Sejuk Beli, Block E1, Bukit Kayu Hitam Immigration, Customs, Quarantine and Security (ICQS) Complex, yesterday.
The inspection found that the frozen chicken products, categorised as 'Chicken Thigh & Leg Boneless Frozen', had been imported from Thailand.
Further checks revealed that the importer had submitted an import permit issued by the Malaysian Quarantine and Inspection Services Department (MAQIS) that had expired.
The consignment was seized under Section 11(1) of the Malaysian Quarantine and Inspection Services Act 2011 (Act 728).
The case was referred to MAQIS for further action.

MCBA Bukit Kayu Hitam commander Senior Assistant Commissioner Fauzi Mohd Yusof said the agency would not compromise on any violation of the law, particularly involving imports that failed to meet the stipulated requirements and regulations.
"Inspections and monitoring will continue to be stepped up to ensure all goods brought into the country are accompanied by valid permits and documents and comply with the laws in force," he said.
f2786b1f0332322c: PETALING JAYA: The High Court's revised court order allowing Najib Razak to serve his remaining SRC International jail term under house arrest has vindicated Attorney-General Dusuki Mokhtar, says DAP MP RSN Rayer.
The Jelutong MP said the High Court's move to set aside the Nov 6 order of discharge and replace it with a new order today proved that Dusuki did not defy the king's conditional pardon for Najib.
"The revised court order issued today has rectified the errors in the previous order issued by the High Court registry.

"This proves that the AG adopted the correct legal procedure in seeking legal clarification about the error in the initial order after the RM50 million fine was paid. The AG did not betray the king's decree.
"The AG must now charge all those who lodged false police reports accusing him of betraying the king, including (Umno supreme council member) Ahmad Maslan," Rayer said in a statement.
Earlier today, Justice Aslam Zainuddin voided the Nov 6 order of discharge on payment of fine on grounds it contravened the conditional pardon granted by the king.
The Attorney-General's Chambers had called for the order to be deferred pending clarification of conflicting terms in the court order.

Istana Negara then warned that challenging the conditional pardon order for Najib would amount to defying the king's authority. Umno and PAS's youth wings later lodged police reports against Dusuki, calling for an investigation into allegations that the AG had abused his powers.
Ahmad, the deputy works minister, also lodged a police report, which he said was to urge the AGC to withdraw its attempt at deferring Najib's house arrest.
bab0e94edc570a2f: KUALA LUMPUR: Several vehicles believed to be carrying family members of former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak arrived at his residence in Langgak Duta here tonight.
The vehicles arrived at 7.55pm, about an hour after a Prisons Department vehicle was seen arriving at the residence.

The arrivals come after the High Court today ordered Najib to serve the remainder of his six-year prison sentence in the SRC International Sdn Bhd case under house arrest at the residence, with immediate effect.
High Court judge Datuk Aslam Zainuddin made the ruling after setting aside an order issued against Najib by the High Court Criminal Registry on Nov 6.

Under the order, Najib will remain under house arrest until Aug 23, 2028, before returning to Kajang Prison on Aug 24, 2028, to serve his separate prison sentence in connection with the 1Malaysia Development Berhad (1MDB) case.
The Home Ministry has said it is ready to implement the court's decision.

Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the ministry respected the royal pardon granted by the Yang di-Pertuan Agong, Sultan Ibrahim, and would ensure that all decisions concerning detention and sentence enforcement were carried out in accordance with the law and valid court orders.
2dc0d5530e9db25a: PETALING JAYA: Rosmah Mansor has expressed gratitude following the fresh High Court order allowing former prime minister Najib Razak to serve the remainder of his SRC International jail sentence under house arrest.
"Thank God," Najib's wife briefly said, according to Berita Harian.
The Malay daily reported that Rosmah was awaiting Najib's return to their home in Jalan Langgak Duta, Taman Duta, Kuala Lumpur, this evening.

Earlier today, the High Court set aside its Nov 6 order of discharge issued following Najib's payment of the RM50 million fine.
It then issued a new order allowing the former prime minister to serve the remainder of his SRC jail term under house arrest from today until Aug 23, 2028.

Najib was jailed in August 2022 after the Federal Court upheld his conviction for abuse of power, criminal breach of trust and money laundering involving RM42 million in SRC funds. He was sentenced to 12 years behind bars and fined RM210 million.
In January 2024, then Yang di-Pertuan Agong, Al-Sultan Abdullah Sultan Ahmad Shah halved Najib’s prison sentence and reduced his fine to RM50 million as part of a royal pardon.

In September this year, the current Yang di-Pertuan Agong, Sultan Ibrahim, granted Najib a further conditional pardon, allowing him to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest until Aug 23, 2028.
The arrangement was subject to Najib paying the RM50 million fine and complying with other stipulated conditions.

Last Friday, the High Court issued the order of discharge on payment of fine but the Attorney-General's Chambers subsequently raised an issue with the document, questioning the accuracy of the terminology and legal provisions used in the document.
b1a55ec1459845c6: WASHINGTON: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's affair with a Chinese businesswoman alleged to be a spy for Beijing facilitated the shipment of at least US$7.5 billion worth of the company's chips to Chinese firms, The Information reported on Tuesday, citing two people who know her.
Alice Huang, along with her husband and sister, built a network of companies across China and Singapore to acquire Nvidia chips, according to the report. Alice Huang and Jensen Huang are not related.

At the centre of the network was Shanghai Century Litong, a China-based company founded in June 2023 that secured preferred cloud partner status with Nvidia by October, giving it priority access to the company's chips, The Information reported.

Century Litong was initially linked to Alice Huang's sister, Huang Yu, through a founding shareholder that was ultimately controlled by Huang Yu before exiting the company in 2024, according to the report.

When orders for Nvidia chips subject to US export restrictions stalled, Alice Huang used ties to Nvidia and its distributors to secure supplies, helping move about 240,000 H100, H200 and some A100 chips into China, the report said.

Century Litong rented computing capacity and operated data centres using Nvidia chips, including some barred from sale to China. Some of the chips ultimately served Alibaba, Tencent and smaller Chinese AI labs, The Information reported.

Alice Huang also held an executive position at Singapore-registered Megaspeed, which was linked to Century Litong and has been investigated by US authorities over Nvidia chip shipments from Southeast Asia to China, the report said.

Megaspeed obtained Nvidia chips by renting computing capacity from Southeast Asian data centres to Chinese customers or by physically shipping hardware into China. Hardware acquired by Speedmatrix, a Malaysian subsidiary established by Megaspeed in 2024, later reached Century Litong, according to The Information.
The report said Alice Huang, also known as Huang Le, leveraged her relationship with Jensen Huang to build credibility while remaining vague about her role and avoiding a paper trail.

Nvidia did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment. Alibaba, Tencent, Megaspeed and Shanghai Century Litong were not immediately available for comment outside regular business hours. Reuters could not independently verify the report.

Nvidia's board on Sunday launched an internal investigation, while the FBI is examining whether 63-year-old Jensen Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence operation. Huang has told employees he was unfaithful to his wife but provided no details about the relationship.
82fda640970b5538: Impervious to battlefield jamming, drones physically connected to human operators by miles of fiber-optic cables have become such a common weapon of war in Ukraine that trees and fields are strewn with tangled cables thinner than fishing lines. But importing such fiber-optic material from China has become more costly as drone warfare’s needs compete with global demand from AI data centers for the same limited supply—and so Ukrainian drone makers have been adapting.

Since the full-scale Russian invasion of Ukraine began in February 2022, the Ukrainians have been forced out of necessity to continually develop battlefield innovations involving first-person view (FPV) quadcopter drones and other heavier types of drones. But it was the Russian military that first deployed unjammable fiber-optic drones to repel Ukrainian forces’ cross-border incursion into the Kursk Oblast in 2024. The Ukrainians quickly followed suit in developing their own fiber-optic drones, given the drones’ capability to shrug off electronic warfare jamming that could neutralize radio-controlled drones.

Russia and Ukraine have relied on Chinese suppliers for some off-the-shelf drones and a wide array of drone components, including bulk orders of fiber wound around very large spools or sometimes small finished spools ready for installation on drones. The finished spools can hold enough fiber-optic cable for drones to regularly operate at ranges of dozens of miles, and sometimes up to 62 miles (100 kilometers) in extreme cases, as reported by the independent Russian publication The Insider.
0480934bd106b31a: KUALA LUMPUR: Najib Razak’s lawyer Shafee Abdullah says only the courts have the authority to draft orders in criminal matters.

He was responding to political commentator Liyana Marzuki’s claim that his firm, Shafee & Co, was responsible for drafting the order of discharge issued following the payment of the RM50 million fine to allow Najib to serve the remainder of his jail sentence under house arrest.

“From what I saw, the drafting was not bad except for a couple of typos. We understood it, the court understood it; only the AGC did not,” he said.

Earlier today, the High Court set aside its previous order discharging the former prime minister upon payment of a RM50 million fine and issued a new order allowing Najib to serve the remainder of his prison sentence in the SRC International case under house arrest.
Justice Aslam Zainuddin made the ruling after hearing the AGC’s application for clarification concerning the “erroneous” Nov 6 order of discharge.

Najib was jailed in August 2022 after the Federal Court upheld his conviction for abuse of power, criminal breach of trust and money laundering involving SRC funds worth RM42 million. He was subsequently sentenced to 12 years behind bars and fined RM210 million.
In January 2024, then Yang di-Pertuan Agong, Al-Sultan Abdullah Sultan Ahmad Shah halved Najib’s prison sentence and reduced his fine to RM50 million as part of a royal pardon.

The current Yang di-Pertuan Agong, Sultan Ibrahim granted Najib a further conditional pardon in September this year, allowing him to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest until Aug 23, 2028, provided he paid the RM50 million fine and complied with other stipulated conditions.

b7e3b6af7af2862a: PUTRAJAYA: The Home Ministry is ready to implement the High Court's decision ordering former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak to serve the remainder of his six-year prison sentence under house arrest until Aug 23, 2028.

7ef6ec4ad6b6bc6d: I've written more than once about the weird positioning of Apple's entry-level 14-inch MacBook Pro, which has always occupied an uncomfortable perch between the MacBook Air and the higher-end MacBook Pros. The best versions of this laptop, like last year's M5 refresh, come with the same basic design and external features of the higher-end MacBook Pros, just with a more modest processor and a lower ceiling for specs like RAM and storage.

The lesser versions stick with older designs or other compromises, reserving Apple's most updated designs and screen technologies for the more expensive high-end models. Recall the 13-inch M1 and M2 MacBook Pros, which stuck with Apple's 2016-era MacBook Pro designs for everything, up to and including the now-abandoned Touch Bar. (If you're someone at Apple maintaining Touch Bar support into the 2030s for the sake of these two laptop models, I'd like to hear from you. Not for a story! I'd just like to know how you are.)

This year's entry-level MacBook Pro mostly falls into that latter category. It does get an Apple M6 chip, and the M6 is great—rumors suggest the M6 won't get Pro, Max, or Ultra configurations, so there are some fringe benefits here that you can't get in the top-tier MacBook Pros. But it uses the same MacBook Pro design Apple has been using since 2021. There's no touchscreen, no OLED panel, no Dynamic Island, no half-pound weight reduction, no glowing Apple logo on the lid.
6d92126aa613cf08: SEOUL: First, BTS packed Stanford Stadium with thousands of screaming fans. Now, their leader RM is inspiring students at the prestigious university to hit the books — and perhaps take a relaxing bike ride while they're at it.

Stanford University is offering a three-credit undergraduate course inspired by the BTS frontman's famously wholesome lifestyle, taking the art of "Namjooning" from ARMY fandom to academia, the Malay Mail reported.
Titled "Namjooning, and Other Well-Being Inspiration from BTS", the introductory psychology seminar explores mental health, happiness and the everyday habits that lead to a more fulfilling life.
For the uninitiated, "Namjooning" is a term coined by fans to describe RM's favourite ways of unwinding, from cycling and visiting art museums to reading, journalling and spending time in nature.
Named after the rapper's real name, Kim Namjoon, the term has become something of a lifestyle mantra among ARMYs, encouraging fans to slow down and appreciate life's simpler pleasures.

Rather than simply advising students to get more sleep, for instance, the course looks at how much sleep people actually need, whether naps help, and what scientific evidence says about building healthier habits.
The course is taught by James R. Jacobs, an associate professor of psychiatry and behavioural sciences.

RM's influence reaches well beyond K-pop.

His enthusiasm recently led to a landmark partnership with the San Francisco Museum of Modern Art.
On Oct 3, the museum launched RM x SFMOMA: Between You and Me, a co-curated exhibition showcasing nearly 200 pieces from both RM's private collection and the museum's own holdings.
e15883ed7bcf6381: Google DeepMind researchers have completed a formal verification of Signal's messaging security, marking what they claim is the first time AI has helped devise a proof that links protocol-level security guarantees to a widely used cryptographic implementation.

They did so using AlphaProof Code, a multi-agent framework for formal software specification and verification. AlphaProof Code relies on a human-guided agent that writes a Lean specification, assesses machine code semantics, and crafts an agent-authored proof that the Lean kernel checks against the specification.

In this instance, AlphaProof Code verified Signal’s post-quantum PQXDH handshake and Triple Ratchet, thereby validating the design of libsignal's forward secrecy, authentication, post-compromise security, and handshake secrecy.

In so doing, the Google/DeepMind team – Swarat Chaudhuri, Andrew Ferraiuolo, Anton Kovsharov, Tej Chajed, Sam Schlesinger, Karn Seth, Jonathan Katz, Charles Sutton, and Pushmeet Kohli – has taken a step toward a challenge the Beneficial AI Foundation issued in April to formally verify the Signal protocol and Signal app with Lean.

The AlphaProof Code process involves working with various models to turn Signal's security goals into a human-reviewed mathematical specification. Based on this spec, the researchers assigned Gemini Carbon agents to generate Lean code proving the correctness of the libsignal implementation. After the agents generated 6.5 million lines of Lean code, they undertook an auditing pass and flagged bits that required human review.
The result is theoretical in that it assumes perfect cryptography and doesn't guarantee the computational secrecy of bytes. But it's still a meaningful assertion of correctness.

"It's a system that is fundamentally built for human AI collaboration," said Swarat Chaudhuri, research scientist at Google DeepMind and a professor at the University of Texas at Austin, in an interview with The Register.

Traditionally, said Chaudhuri, you start proving theorems with well-defined problems formulated by a mathematician that get submitted to an AI agent for proof. In this case, the researchers had to figure out what to prove.

"In formal methods, we always had this belief that verification is the hard bit," he said. "There's thirty or forty years of work on how to scale up verification. Now we are able to do that. So now the question is what are we verifying? … That process is fundamentally human-in-the-loop, but we devised a process of trying to scale it up to the extent possible with AI."

As Chaudhuri and his colleagues note in their research paper, "AlphaProof Code: Verifying Signal’s Security at the Machine-Code Level," formal verification used to require heroic efforts. Formally verifying the seL4 microkernel took 20 person-years, while developing the verified CompCert C compiler took six years.
AlphaProof Code, they believe, can drastically reduce the cost of formal verification, though their Signal work still took four weeks for a team of five people and "quite a few tokens."

"The dream is definitely to scale this up," said Chaudhuri. "So you know there's been this rise in offensive AI capabilities, right? There are a lot of insecure systems around the world, and they're going to be exploited.

"So what we really need to do is to apply this kind of technology to code at large all over the world and figure out what is it that you want to guard against? How do you write those properties, how do we specify those properties? That's going to be super important, but we have to figure that out."

Pointing to a related DeepMind project, AlphaProof Nexus, which is focused on mathematics, Chaudhuri said the next step is to apply this technology during the software design process – not just to cryptographic protocols but code in general.

"We really believe that the next frontier is not going to be proof but specification in this kind of research," he said. "And so that's why we took on this domain where that was actually a hard problem. And I think that we have some really good insights now about how to go about this, although not the last word by any means." ®
f60b51a297eb7c83: MELAKA: Umno president Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has called for an end to the polemics surrounding former prime minister Najib Razak's house arrest, saying all parties must respect the king’s decision and authority enshrined under the Federal Constitution.

Zahid was asked to comment on the Kuala Lumpur High Court’s decision to issue a fresh order allowing Najib to serve the remainder of his prison sentence for his graft conviction under house arrest with immediate effect.
He also expressed hope that Najib would be able to spend time with his family.

e0a09c112df57b81: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 11 — The ringgit ended marginally higher against the US dollar today, supported by improving market sentiment amid expectations of a de-escalation of the US-Iran conflict.

6859bf9331b87487: CARACAS: US oil giant ExxonMobil signed a memorandum of understanding with Venezuela on Monday, as foreign companies scramble for a slice of the country's crude following pressure from Donald Trump to open up the sector.
Venezuela's interim leader Delcy Rodriguez has granted Washington access to a huge chunk of national crude reserves since a US raid toppled president Nicolas Maduro in January.
Venezuela sits on the world's largest proven oil reserves, but years of sanctions, underinvestment and mismanagement have crippled the once booming industry.
The agreement paves the way for ExxonMobil, the world's second-biggest oil company, to develop oil fields containing billions of barrels in reserves.
ExxonMobil has not operated in Venezuela since 2007, when late socialist leader Hugo Chavez seized its assets as part of a widespread expropriation campaign.

The "significant" agreement is "the result of months of negotiations aimed at the effective return of ExxonMobil to hydrocarbon operations" within the country, Rodriguez said during a televised address.

Dan Ammann, president of ExxonMobil Upstream Company, said, "We believe that the unique combination of ExxonMobil's capabilities, the extraordinary resources of this country and our partnership will result in significant benefits for all stakeholders."

Critics in both the US and Venezuela accuse Trump of holding the country to ransom after ousting Maduro and warn that Rodriguez could face a similar fate if she does not give in to Washington's demands.
Rodriguez insists Venezuela retains control of its oil.
fa765491221f1b26: KUALA LUMPUR: Sunway Real Estate Investment Trust (Reit) today reported a lower net profit of RM116.17 million in the third quarter ended Sept 30, 2026 (Q3 2026) compared to RM121.85 a year earlier.

Sunway Reit Management Sdn Bhd, the manager of Sunway Reit, said the decline in revenue was mainly due to the disposal of Sunway university and college campus in September 2025 in line with its asset recycling strategy, resulting in a one-off gain on disposal of RM25.6 million in Q3 2025.
For the nine-month period ended Sept 30, 2026, net profit dropped to RM331.80 million from RM344.04 million in last year's corresponding period.

Revenue, however, grew to RM675.67 million from RM666.69 million previously, driven by a stronger contribution of RM43.1 million from the retail segment, more than offsetting the absence of RM29.3 million in revenue contribution from Sunway university and college campus.
Sunway Reit Management chief executive officer Derek Teh Wan Wei said Sunway Reit continued to demonstrate the resilience and quality of its diversified portfolio in Q3 2026.
He said the retail segment remained the key growth driver, supported by strong shopper traffic, healthy tenant sales, positive rental reversions and sustained contributions from our retail assets.

Teh said the office segment also delivered improved performance on the back of stronger occupancy and leasing momentum, while the hotel segment experienced temporary headwinds arising from the ongoing conflicts in Middle East and haze-related disruptions in the Klang Valley.
"Looking ahead, we remain cautiously optimistic about Sunway Reit's overall prospects for the remainder of 2026.

"The retail segment is expected to sustain its growth momentum, supported by resilient consumer spending, strong occupancy levels and positive rental reversions, while the office and industrial segments are poised to benefit further from continued leasing momentum and improving occupancy," he said.

For the hotel segment, Teh said, Sunway Reit would remain focused on strengthening performance through proactive marketing and pricing strategies, while enhancing demand across banqueting and MICE activities.

"Moving forward, we will continue to prioritise proactive asset management, operational efficiency and sustainable growth to enhance portfolio resilience and deliver long-term value to our unitholders," he said.
Sunway Reit owns a diversified portfolio of 28 properties comprising 14 retail properties, six hotels, five offices and three industrial properties, with a combined property value of RM10.3 billion.

Saifuddin concluded by saying that the federal government would continue to defend the Malay rulers’ role and position within the framework of Malaysia’s constitutional monarchy, while upholding constitutional supremacy, rule of law and the judiciary’s independence.
“These principles complete each other and are the basis for national stability,” he concluded.

While Najib will be able to serve the rest of his SRC International jail term at home until August 23, 2028, he is also facing a separate 15-year jail term in his other trial involving over RM2 billion of 1Malaysia Development Berhad (1MDB) funds.

9d5ff885fe31630c: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 10 — The Attorney General’s Chambers (AGC) today sought to ensure that Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s house arrest arrangements explicitly provided for his return to Kajang Prison on August 24, 2028, to serve his separate 1Malaysia Development Berhad (1MDB) prison sentence.

In its written application, the prosecution requested that the High Court replace a November 6 discharge order with new terms clarifying Najib’s remaining SRC International sentence and his subsequent imprisonment in the 1MDB case.
The application specified that Najib should “be transferred back to Kajang Prison on August 24, 2028, to serve the sentence imposed on him in the 1MDB case”.
It also sought to specify that his SRC sentence would end on August 23, 2028, with his return to prison subject to any court order then in force.
The prosecution said the 1MDB prison sentence had been directed to begin once his SRC sentence ended, arguing that “the end date of the SRC sentences must be stated with certainty”.

It explained that Najib’s payment of the RM50 million fine on November 6 discharged his liability for the fine and imprisonment for non-payment, but did not extinguish his remaining SRC prison sentence.

The AGC also argued that the earlier discharge order, which used a standard form for release upon payment of a fine, could be interpreted as releasing Najib from his remaining SRC sentence altogether.
Citing provisions of the Criminal Procedure Code governing imprisonment warrants, the prosecution said there was an urgent need for a clear order in accordance with the law.

High Court judge Datuk Aslam Zainuddin subsequently granted the prosecution’s application, setting aside the November 6 discharge order and allowing Najib to serve the remainder of his SRC sentence under house arrest until August 23, 2028.
According to Bernama, Judge Aslam said the court would replace the earlier order “entirely with the order sought in this application”.
The new order also provides for Najib’s return to Kajang Prison on August 24, 2028, to serve his separate 1MDB sentence, Bernama reported.

At the hearing, Najib’s lead counsel Tan Sri Muhammad Shafee Abdullah had argued that the original discharge order was already clear, as the RM50 million fine required under the conditional royal pardon had been paid.
Speaking to reporters afterwards, Shafee welcomed the court’s clarification despite maintaining that the original order was sound.

a40a811f43d077dd: BANGKOK: Thailand's cabinet agreed new rules on noise and water use for data centres on Tuesday, after a review sparked by public concern over an AI-driven construction boom.
"The use of national resources must not adversely affect the public," finance minister Ekniti Nitithanprapas told a news conference.
The government said in September it would tighten oversight of data centres, asking developers of nearly 50 under-construction projects to pause work until new rules were drawn up.
Proposed standards include limiting noise at site boundaries to 70 A-weighted decibels (dBA), according to a government data centre board.
That is slightly quieter than a vacuum cleaner, according to a comparison chart published by Yale University.
The government also proposed capping nearby temperature increases to 1°C to 2°C and said cooling water must be recirculated and tested before discharge.
New zoning rules were also approved in principle, with centres consuming more than 20 megawatts of energy set to be located in industrial zones and face stricter oversight.
Narit Therdsteerasukdi, from Thailand's Board of Investment, said 57 data centre projects have been approved across the country.
Seventeen are operating, 20 have received construction permits and 20 are preparing to invest.
Ekniti said the government also received a large number of speculative applications.
More than 110 applicants had requested over 30,000 megawatts of electricity, he said, but only about a quarter or fewer had genuine investment plans.
Eligible projects approved before August 14 will have one year to meet environmental guidelines.

7f5b2df7ca43170b: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 10 — For some Malaysian Chinese youths, deciding where to study after secondary school is not simply a matter of choosing a course or university.
Most of these choices are made through weighing how secure they feel about their chances of getting into their preferred programme.

In a research conducted by IMAN Research, they found that uncertainty over public university admissions, differences between pre-university pathways and concerns about access to certain courses had influenced how some the research participants approached their education.

In its recently published report, Kami Orang Sini Juga: Chinese Youths and Democratic Belonging — The Politics of Pragmatism and Fairness, draws on interviews with 116 Malaysian Chinese youths aged between 18 and 35 across Peninsular Malaysia.

The study found that education was one of the areas where participants’ perceptions of fairness were particularly shaped by their own experiences, expectations and accounts they had heard from others.
Some participants described choosing private education or overseas study rather than applying through the public university admission system.

One interviewee, for instance, went directly to a private university without applying through the Unit Pusat Universiti (UPU), citing concerns within the family about the chances of securing a place through the public route.
Another participant who wanted to study medicine declined an offer to pursue biotechnology and instead went to China.
The report describes these decisions as examples of how young people may seek alternatives when public pathways appear uncertain.

However, it also makes an important distinction between barriers participants personally experienced, obstacles they anticipated and accounts they had heard from family members or their wider community.
These are not the same kinds of evidence, and the researchers cautioned against treating every disappointing outcome or decision not to apply as proof of discrimination.
Matriculation and UPU are not the same
The research found that there was a recurring source of confusion among participants — the relationship between the matriculation quota and university admissions through UPU.
The report clarifies that the 90 per cent Bumiputera quota applies to entry into matriculation, not to UPU’s university selection formula.
UPU ranks applicants from STPM, matriculation and other equivalent qualifications using 90 per cent academic marks and 10 per cent co-curricular marks.
Candidates are considered according to merit, programme requirements, available places and their course preferences.
The report said the UPU pathway itself does not have an ethnic quota system.
However, the researchers noted that differences between Sijil Tinggi Persekolahan Malaysia (STPM) and matriculation could still raise questions about fairness.
STPM generally takes one and a half years, while the main matriculation programme takes one year.
The two pathways also use different assessment structures.
How are they different?
STPM students may progress through school, zone, district, state and national competitions, while matriculation students compete within a structure centred on inter-college competitions.

Citing figures that showed 16 per cent of matriculation students achieved a cumulative grade point average of 4.0, compared with 3.09 per cent of STPM students, the researchers suggest these differences be examined when considering how students from the two pathways are assessed

For popular courses such as medicine, pharmacy and dentistry at public universities, matriculation students accounted for more than 97 per cent of places in 2023, while STPM students made up less than 3 per cent, according to figures cited in the report.
These figures were used to illustrate differences in outcomes between the pathways, rather than establish that any individual applicant had been unfairly treated.
When students look for alternatives
The report found that family resources played an important role in determining whether young people could pursue alternatives when they felt uncertain about public education pathways.
Some could afford private universities or overseas study, while others had fewer options.
This meant that the ability to work around perceived barriers was not equally available to everyone.
The researchers also noted that concerns inherited from parents or community members could influence decisions even before a student applied for a place.
In such cases, these Chinese youths people might rule out a pathway based on what they had heard about the system, rather than on a direct experience of rejection.
The report recommends that the government make university admissions criteria, selection mechanisms and intake data more transparent and accessible.
It also calls for students to be given clearer information about how different pre-university qualifications are assessed and how they affect university options.

The researchers said differences in co-curricular opportunities between STPM and matriculation should also be reviewed, alongside clearer pathways for students holding the Unified Examination Certificate who wish to enter public universities.
Rather than redesigning the entire pre-university system, the report suggests addressing specific areas where the students face uncertainty or unequal opportunities.

Its broader concern is that when students cannot clearly understand how public education pathways work, they may make decisions based on assumptions, family experiences or perceived limitations — potentially narrowing their choices before they have fully explored them.

e830fec390fbe916: KUALA LUMPUR: Foreign holdings of Malaysian bonds posted a strong inflow in October, signalling confidence in Malaysia's economic fundamentals.

"Foreign holdings saw a significant increase in the final week of October, reaching a record high.

The firm said the US Treasury (UST) yield curve experienced a flattening last month, averaging around 5.12 per cent on the back of heightened geopolitical risk and expectations for a delayed rate hike.

However, yields steadily eased lower through the remainder of the month.

Downward momentum accelerated following the announcement made by the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) announcement, where it voted 10–2 to hold the fed funds target rate steady at 3.75 per cent–4.00 per cent.

"The split decision signalled a hawkish hold, reinforcing the possibility of further monetary tightening, although the US Federal Reserve (Fed) opted to assess incoming economic data before its next policy decision.
"Nevertheless, market expectations remain tilted toward a potential 25 basis points (bps) rate hike at the upcoming FOMC meeting in December," said the firm.

"Concurrently, we expect the continuous hawkish outlook for the US fed funds rate has led markets to price in a hawkish and 'higher-for-longer' policy stance.
"Investors anticipate a 25bps rate hike at the upcoming FOMC meeting in December.

0fcbea18e04ed1dc: KUALA LUMPUR: Big Caring Group Bhd's initial public offering (IPO) has been priced at RM1.08 per share, with its public tranche oversubscribed 4.31 times ahead of its listing on Bursa Malaysia's Main Market.
The final retail price of RM1.08 matches the institutional price determined through the bookbuilding process, with no refund required for successful retail applicants.
Malaysian Issuing House Sdn Bhd said the public portion, comprising 147.64 million shares, received 29,474 applications for 783.75 million shares.
The Bumiputera portion attracted 7,266 applications for 142.85 million shares, representing an oversubscription rate of 0.94 times.
Meanwhile, the other Malaysian public portion received 22,208 applications for 640.9 million shares, translating into an oversubscription rate of 7.68 times.
The 120 million shares allocated to eligible directors, employees and other contributors to the group were fully subscribed after applying the relevant clawback and reallocation provisions.
The institutional offering of 1.61 billion shares to Malaysian and foreign institutional and selected investors was also fully subscribed.
Of the institutional offering, 19 cornerstone investors subscribed for 41.2 per cent.
Big Caring's IPO involves up to 1.88 billion shares, comprising an offer for sale of 1.29 billion existing shares and a public issue of 590.55 million new shares.
It is poised to become Malaysia's second-largest IPO of 2026 by market capitalisation, with a valuation of about RM8 billion ahead of its Main Market debut on Nov 19.
At that valuation, Big Caring will rank behind Sunway Healthcare Holdings Bhd, which made its market debut in March with an IPO valuation of RM16.68 billion.
It will also be more than three times the size of MTT Shipping and Logistics Bhd, which was valued at RM2.58 billion when it listed in April.
The notices of allotment will be mailed to successful applicants by Nov 18.
Maybank Investment Bank Bhd and RHB Investment Bank Bhd are the joint principal advisers, joint global coordinators, joint bookrunners, joint managing underwriters and joint underwriters for the IPO.
AmInvestment Bank Bhd is also a joint principal adviser, joint global coordinator, joint bookrunner and joint underwriter.
UBS Securities Malaysia Sdn Bhd and UBS AG, Singapore Branch are joint global coordinators and joint bookrunners.
0147863b12c69457: KUALA LUMPUR: Legal questions over the interpretation of the conditional pardon order and a subsequent discharge order had delayed the implementation of Datuk Seri Najib Razak's house arrest, said Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail.

Responding to the High Court's decision today allowing the former prime minister to serve the remainder of his SRC International sentence under house arrest, Saifuddin said the ruling had clarified the legal issues.
He said questions surrounding the conditional pardon order and the Nov 6 discharge order, particularly the provision for house arrest, had held up its implementation.

Saifuddin said the ministry was now ready to implement the court's decision to set aside the Nov 6 order for Najib's discharge upon payment of a fine and allow him to serve the remainder of his six-year sentence under house arrest until Aug 23, 2028.
"In this regard, the ministry respects the Attorney-General's Chambers' position that these questions should be clarified through judicial proceedings.
"This approach is important to ensure that every government action has a clear, orderly and lawful legal basis," he said.
He said the ministry and the Prisons Department would ensure that all decisions on the implementation of sentences and detention complied with the law and valid court orders.

"The ministry has always respected and upheld royal pardon decisions granted by His Majesty the Yang di-Pertuan Agong, in accordance with the powers vested under Article 42 of the Federal Constitution.
"Every decision made through constitutional channels must be respected and implemented in accordance with the law," he said.
Article 42 of the Federal Constitution provides for the power to grant pardons, reprieves, respites and remissions, as well as to suspend or commute sentences.
Saifuddin described the case as high-profile, with significant political implications and public interest, and urged all parties to handle it responsibly.
He said political polemics should not undermine public confidence in the country's institutions.

"The government will continue to uphold the position and role of the Malay Rulers within the framework of a constitutional monarchy, while safeguarding the supremacy of the Constitution, the rule of law and the independence of the judiciary.
"These principles complement one another and form the foundation of the country's stability," he said.
aa7da1e6d9c493bb: PETALING JAYA: MISC Bhd’s proposal to acquire and privatise Yinson Holdings Bhd via a consortium would increase its financial risk, a research house said.
CGS International warned that the energy infrastructure group's heavy gearing leaves shareholders particularly “exposed to project execution risks”.
“Yinson is very highly geared, and its operational execution needs to be almost perfect for its shareholders to secure positive returns,” said CGS in a research note.

It put Yinson’s net gearing at 1.1 times as at July 31, rising to 3.1 times under its assessment if perpetual securities and redeemable convertible preference shares (RCPS) were reclassified from equity to debt.
It said, though, that this financial structure could amplify returns from Yinson’s future contract wins, it also “accentuates the risk to shareholders”.

A slowdown in awards for floating production, storage and offloading (FPSO) vessels could also delay those gains, said CGS, while questioning whether paying cash was the best way for Petronas-controlled MISC to expand its offshore business.

Last Friday, MISC together with Yinson’s founding Lim family and the Employees Provident Fund (EPF) proposed to take Yinson private at RM2.50 a share, a 10.6% premium to its closing price of RM2.26 on Nov 6.
The acquisition of the remaining 55.2% stake in Yinson will entail a cash consideration of RM4.03 billion, valuing the group at RM7.31 billion.

The transaction will be undertaken through MY Offshore Holdings Sdn Bhd (MYOH), in which MISC and Yinson Legacy Sdn Bhd (YLSB), the investment vehicle of Yinson executive chairman Lim Han Weng, will each hold a 41.46% stake, while EPF will retain an effective 17.07% stake.

MISC will inject RM3.03 billion into MYOH to acquire the shares while YLSB, which owns 27.73% of Yinson, will transfer its stake to MYOH and contribute the remaining RM1 billion in cash. EPF will only roll over its shares. The acquisition is expected to be completed in the second half of 2027.

MISC plans to finance about three-quarters of its RM3.03 investment through new borrowings amounting to RM2.27 billion, with the remainder funded internally. At end-June, the oil and gas shipping company had RM7.2 billion in cash, deposits and bank balances, against total borrowings of RM12.96 billion.
CGS maintained its “reduce” recommendation on MISC with a RM7.58 target price. The stock fell 2 sen or 0.25% to RM7.99 today, valuing it at RM35.67 billion.

Meanwhile, TA Research said the acquisition is expected to increase MISC’s pro forma gearing from 0.36 times to 0.43 times, reflecting the additional borrowings required to fund approximately 75% of its RM3 billion investment.

It noted the additional debt will raise MISC’s financing commitments, with the returns from Yinson needing to sufficiently compensate for the associated funding costs. The transaction is also unlikely to materially enhance MISC's near-term earnings, the research house added.

Analysts agree that MISC’s investment provides it with exposure to Yinson’s established FPSO platform alongside an offshore contracted revenue backlog of approximately US$19.3 billion (RM78.3 billion).

Yinson was founded by Lim, 73, and his wife Bah Kim Lian in 1984, as a lorry transport company before diversifying into the oil and gas sector. It is now one of the world’s biggest providers of FPSO vessels, which are used to extract and store crude oil.

7156c96ea3142782: The European Union has dragged IBM, Atos, and Leonardo into court over years of delays to its troubled €212 million smart border system, which finally went live after missing a string of deadlines and leaving travelers stuck in airport queues.
The lawsuit dates back to December 22, 2025, when eu-LISA, the agency behind the EU's fingerprint-and-facial-image border checks for non-EU travelers, filed its claim in an Estonian court.

The lawsuit was buried in eu-LISA's 2025 financial accounts, published in July, with no mention of who was being sued. The Financial Times has since named the three companies after obtaining letters exchanged with the agency.
In a statement to The Register, eu-LISA confirmed it had initiated proceedings "in line with the Agency’s responsibility to protect the EU’s financial interests."

"The proceedings concern the system’s development phase and have no impact on its current operation. EES (entry exit system) is fully operational," the agency said, declining to discuss the ongoing case.

The EES was supposed to be ready in 2022 yet wasn't live until October 2025 and was only fully operational from April. Travelers have since had to contend with hours-long airport queues and fingerprint scanners that reportedly struggle with sweaty fingers. Behind the scenes, things weren't going much better, with the consortium and eu-LISA spending years arguing over missed deadlines, financial penalties and who was to blame.

IBM Belgium and Atos Belgium were already arguing over penalties back in October 2021, when they disputed a fine from eu-LISA and pointed to the COVID-19 pandemic and other factors beyond their control as reasons for the delays.
By February 2022, the consortium was pushing back against another set of deadlines, warning that the agency's timetable was unrealistic.

"Ignoring reality is not prudent and will not help to achieve the plan," the companies wrote, according to the FT. "On the contrary, working with an unrealistic plan will cause frustration for all stakeholders."
The consortium also criticized eu-LISA's "overall governance," suggesting relations between the two sides had become rather frosty.
The fallout wasn't cheap. The contract had already grown from €142 million to €212 million in 2021, and the delays kept adding to the bill.

In its 2022 accounts [PDF], eu-LISA acknowledged difficulties with the consortium and warned of additional costs, with the setbacks also holding up other EU IT projects. By 2023, it had nearly doubled its annual EES budget to €40 million by diverting funds from elsewhere, partly to cover rising hardware and software maintenance costs.
The FT also reported that IBM agreed in March 2022 to let eu-LISA withhold certain payments while the dispute over damages was resolved.
The original contract expired last year, with a new consortium taking over implementation, although IBM, Atos, and Leonardo remained responsible until August.

The project has attracted scrutiny for more than its ballooning budget. Last year, Atos reportedly used its Moscow office to procure software for the system, raising questions about Russian involvement in sensitive European border infrastructure.

The EU's anti-fraud office, OLAF, found sufficient grounds for further investigation, according to an internal report seen by the FT. However, it referred the matter back to eu-LISA despite describing the agency's initial assessment as insufficient.
Estonia's Harju County Court confirmed that the civil case had been filed, although no hearings have taken place or been scheduled.
IBM and Atos did not respond to The Register's questions.
The EES may finally be up and running, but the argument over who should foot the bill for getting it there looks far from settled. ®
